title: Find out whether a tool letter fires while an inspector field has the keyboard
goal: When you click into one of the number fields in the right hand panel and start typing, a letter may be taken as a tool shortcut instead of going into the field: pressing T there switched to the Text tool and pressing X swapped the fill colours. It is not yet known whether that happens in the real app or only in the scripted test runner, which can never be the active app. Find out which, because if it is real then typing into any panel field is unsafe.
notes:
ANSWERED 2026-09-08: the app is fine, the walk was wrong.

Evidence, from a probe launched normally with a file and brought to the front (app active true, editor window key true):
  Scripts/build-app.sh --probe
  open -a "$PWD/dist/Photonz Probe.app" "$PWD/Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/Fixtures/settings-pane-2x.png" --args --shortcut-diag
  cat /tmp/photonz-shortcut-diag.txt
printed:
  app active: true; activation policy: accessory; editor window is key: true
  t via sendEvent with nothing in the panel focused: tool text -> SHORTCUT FIRED (the Text tool)
  x via sendEvent with nothing in the panel focused: fills #FFFFFF/#000000 -> SHORTCUT FIRED (the fill colours swapped)
  t via sendEvent with the W field holding the keyboard: field holds "t" (the letter LANDED), tool select -> no shortcut
  x via sendEvent with the W field holding the keyboard: field holds "x" (the letter LANDED), tool select, fills #000000/#FFFFFF -> no shortcut
  t via performKeyEquivalent with the W field holding the keyboard: nothing typed, tool text -> SHORTCUT FIRED
  x via performKeyEquivalent with the W field holding the keyboard: nothing typed, fills #FFFFFF/#000000 -> SHORTCUT FIRED

So the real dispatch (NSApplication.sendEvent) decides "typing, not a shortcut" before any key equivalent is offered, and the same press fires both shortcuts the moment the field lets go. The harness key step was calling window.performKeyEquivalent by hand for the keyDown, skipping that decision, which is where the report came from. The CoreGraphics postToPid press never arrived in either run, so read that line as no answer rather than as no shortcut.

SECOND RUN 2026-09-08 added the shift case, measured the same way:
  ⇧M via sendEvent, nothing focused -> SHORTCUT FIRED (tool select -> rectSelect)
  ⇧M via sendEvent, W field holding the keyboard -> field holds "M" (LANDED), tool stayed select -> no shortcut
  ⇧M via performKeyEquivalent, W field holding the keyboard -> nothing typed, tool ellipseSelect -> SHORTCUT FIRED
So shift is a typing modifier, and the first fix's "no modifiers at all" rule left the same bug reachable via ⇧M, which the app really does bind (EditorView.swift:2423, cycle the selection tool).

Landed: PlaytestHarness.isTyping (a field editor has the keyboard, nothing but shift held, and the press would insert a character) short-circuits to window.sendEvent and logs "taken by the field being typed in". Narrowed on purpose to inserting characters: Return, Escape, Tab, the arrows, delete and the function keys are key equivalents in the real app even mid-edit (a sheet answers Return with its default button while the caret is in a box), so they are untouched, as are all modified chords. expect field also fixed: it read NSTextField.stringValue, which lags a live edit, and now reads the field editor. New walk Scripts/playtest/typing-in-a-field-walk.json holds it. ShortcutDiag lives in Sources/Photonz/Playtest/ShortcutDiag.swift, probe only, documented in docs/design/playtest-harness.md.

Related and consistent: the two done tasks about a number field and a name field handing the keyboard back were about the field never LETTING GO after Return, which is a real and separate thing; nothing there needs revisiting.

Regression test is proven, not assumed: with isTyping forced to return false the walk fails at step 7 with "no field called \"W\" is in the panel to read; the ones that are: Search components" — the T fired the Text tool and swapped the inspector out from under the walk. That is the original report reproduced. The walk's tool claims are waitFor steps now; they were describe steps, which assert nothing, so the walk as first written could not have caught a regression.
acceptance: A written answer, backed by a run, saying whether a tool letter typed into an inspector field reaches the field or fires the shortcut in the REAL app
If it fires the shortcut, letters typed into a focused panel field go into the field and no tool shortcut runs
If it is only an artefact of the scripted runner, the playtest harness notes say so, so no later run files this again

log.note: Adversarial pass before touching anything: the report was a walk log, and a walk is the one place this question cannot be answered. Two confounds, not one: the app is never active in a walk, AND the walk does not press keys the way the system does. The harness `key` step calls window.performKeyEquivalent by hand for the keyDown (PlaytestHarness.press), so it offers the shortcut BEFORE anything gets to decide the press is typing. Real AppKit makes that decision inside NSApplication.sendEvent. So the walk could fire a shortcut the app never would.

Built a probe-only diagnostic to settle it on the real app: --shortcut-diag (Sources/Photonz/Playtest/ShortcutDiag.swift). Launched normally with a file, brings itself to the front, puts the keyboard in the panel W box, presses the letter three ways (NSApp.sendEvent, CGEvent.postToPid, window.performKeyEquivalent), and presses each letter with NOTHING focused first as the control.

ANSWER: it is the scripted runner, not the app. Run of 2026-09-08, app active true, editor window key true. Control: t and x via sendEvent with nothing focused -> SHORTCUT FIRED (Text tool; fills swapped). With the W field holding the keyboard, the same presses via sendEvent -> the letter LANDED in the field, tool stayed select, fills stayed #000000/#FFFFFF. Via performKeyEquivalent (what the walk does) -> nothing typed, SHORTCUT FIRED, both letters. Full output: /tmp/photonz-shortcut-diag.txt.

Fixed the harness rather than only writing it down. PlaytestHarness.press now applies AppKit own rule: no modifiers plus a field editor holding the keyboard means the press is typing, so the key equivalents are not offered and the log says taken by the field being typed in. Modified chords untouched. Also fixed expect field, which read NSTextField.stringValue and so could never see what a key step had just typed; it reads the live field editor now.

Regression walk: Scripts/playtest/typing-in-a-field-walk.json. Types t then x into W (expect W reads t, then tx), then lets the field go and presses t and requires the Text tool. Passes. Scripts/test.sh green: 4844 tests in 411 suites.
runner failed (exit 0, attempt 1): Waiting on the walk suite to finish before the final rebuild, screenshot, audit, and commit.

Resumed after the previous attempt died mid-finalize. Found its walk-suite probe still running and orphaned (pid 27080, contents-for-several-walk.json, 5+ minutes in); quit it with Scripts/probe-app.sh --quit before doing anything else.

Second adversarial pass on the FIX, not the report: the rule shipped as "no modifiers at all is typing", and shift is a modifier. But shift is how a capital letter gets into a name field, and the app hangs a real shortcut on ⇧M (EditorView.swift:2423, cycle the selection tool). So the same false bug was still reachable, just with the shift key held. Measured it rather than reasoning about it: extended ShortcutDiag to press ⇧M as well.

⇧M measured, probe active and key: with nothing focused it cycled the selection tool (select -> rectSelect). With the W field holding the keyboard, sendEvent put "M" in the box and left the tool on select; performKeyEquivalent (the harness's old path) typed nothing and cycled to ellipseSelect. Identical shape to t and x, so shift is typing. Widened isTyping to flags.subtracting(.shift).isEmpty. Command, option and control still go to the key equivalents, so ⌘C over a field is still copy.

Hardened the regression walk, which as written could not have failed: its two "the tool must NOT have changed" claims were describe steps, which assert nothing. Each typing step now carries waitFor tool select, plus a ⇧M step expecting the box to read txM. Proved it is a real test by putting isTyping back to returning false: the walk failed at step 7, "no field called W is in the panel to read; the ones that are: Search components" — T had fired the Text tool and swapped the whole inspector, which is the original report reproduced. Restored, rebuilt, walk ok, 23 steps.

Scripts/test.sh green: 4844 tests in 411 suites. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-08-typing-in-a-panel-field.json with two real screen captures (Screen Recording granted this run), not offscreen renders.
